variants.title: Radioactivity of potassium sulphate with a GM counter
variants.unknown: the count rate above background from the K-40 in potassium sulphate
variants.note: Potassium sulphate is 44.9 % potassium by mass against 52.4 % for the chloride, so the same 100 g gives about 14 % fewer counts. SIMULATED DATA; the tray efficiency is a design value.

source.title: IUPAC standard atomic weights K 39.0983, S 32.06, O 15.999 (mass fraction 2 x 39.0983 / 174.25); K-40 data from NNDC / NUBASE

variants.title: Radioactivity of potassium carbonate with a GM counter
variants.unknown: the count rate above background from the K-40 in potassium carbonate
variants.note: Potassium carbonate is 56.6 % potassium by mass, the richest of the three salts, so it counts the most. SIMULATED DATA; the tray efficiency is a design value.

source.title: IUPAC standard atomic weights K 39.0983, C 12.011, O 15.999 (mass fraction 2 x 39.0983 / 138.20); K-40 data from NNDC / NUBASE
